title: Cardiovascular Risk Score Calculator
problem: Cardiologists must calculate 10-year ASCVD risk scores, Framingham scores, and HEART scores manually or toggle between MDCalc tabs during patient visits. This slows consultations and introduces transcription errors. Incorrect risk stratification can lead to under- or over-treatment of patients.
who: All practicing cardiologists during outpatient consultations

skill_spec.name: Cardio Risk Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates ASCVD 10-year risk, Framingham Risk Score, and HEART score from patient parameters

outputs.name: statin_recommendation
outputs.label: Statin therapy recommendation per ACC/AHA guidelines

skill_spec.formula_hint: Pooled Cohort Equations (2013 ACC/AHA) with race/sex-specific coefficients. Log-transformed variables, Cox regression model. Low <5%, Borderline 5-7.5%, Intermediate 7.5-20%, High >=20%.

example_queries: Calculate ASCVD risk for a 58-year-old white male, total cholesterol 240, HDL 42, systolic BP 148, on BP meds, non-diabetic, non-smoker
What's the 10-year heart risk for a 65-year-old African American woman with diabetes and cholesterol of 210?

title: Drug Dosing & Interaction Calculator for Cardiac Medications
problem: Cardiologists prescribe complex multi-drug regimens (anticoagulants, antiarrhythmics, heart failure drugs) that require weight-based dosing, renal adjustment, and interaction checking. Errors in anticoagulant dosing can cause fatal bleeding or stroke. Calculating CrCl-adjusted doses during a busy clinic is error-prone.
who: All cardiologists prescribing anticoagulants, antiarrhythmics, and heart failure medications

skill_spec.name: Cardiac Drug Dose Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates renal-adjusted doses for cardiac drugs including DOACs, antiarrhythmics, and heart failure medications with interaction warnings
skill_spec.formula_hint: CrCl via Cockcroft-Gault. Dose tables per FDA labeling for each drug. DOAC dosing: apixaban reduce if 2+ of age>=80, weight<=60kg, Cr>=1.5. Amiodarone loading vs maintenance. Check CYP3A4/P-gp interactions.

example_queries: What dose of apixaban for a 82-year-old woman, 55 kg, creatinine 1.6, with AFib?
Calculate amiodarone loading dose for a 90 kg patient with new-onset atrial fibrillation, currently on warfarin and digoxin

title: MIPS Quality Reporting Score Estimator
problem: Cardiologists must report quality measures under CMS MACRA/MIPS or face payment adjustments up to -9%. Tracking performance across 4 categories (Quality, Improvement Activities, Promoting Interoperability, Cost) is complex. Many cardiologists lose thousands in Medicare reimbursement due to poor MIPS scores they didn't track proactively.
who: All cardiologists billing Medicare, especially small/independent practices

skill_spec.name: MIPS Score Estimator
skill_spec.one_liner: Estimates MIPS composite score and projected Medicare payment adjustment based on reported measures

inputs.name: quality_score_avg
inputs.label: Average quality measure performance (0-10 per measure)

skill_spec.formula_hint: Quality=30% weight, Cost=30%, Improvement Activities=15%, Promoting Interoperability=25%. Threshold ~75 for neutral adjustment. Max penalty -9%, max bonus varies. Quality score = sum of decile scores / max possible * 100.

example_queries: Estimate my MIPS score: 6 quality measures averaging 8/10, 4 improvement activities, PI score 85, cost score 60, Medicare revenue $400,000
What payment adjustment will I face with a MIPS composite of 45?

title: Prior Authorization Request Generator
problem: Cardiologists spend 7.3 hours per week on prior authorization and insurance tasks - the single biggest administrative burden. Each prior auth for cardiac procedures (catheterization, stress tests, cardiac MRI, device implantation) requires specific clinical justification language that insurers accept. Denials delay critical cardiac care and can endanger patients.
who: All cardiologists and their support staff dealing with commercial and Medicare Advantage insurers

skill_spec.name: Prior Auth Letter Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates prior authorization letters with clinical justification for cardiac procedures using ACC Appropriate Use Criteria

variables.name: procedure_requested
variables.label: Procedure requested (e.g., cardiac catheterization, cardiac MRI)

variables.name: clinical_summary
variables.label: Brief clinical summary (symptoms, test results, EF if known)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Physician header -> Date/To insurer -> RE: patient info -> Medical necessity statement citing ACC AUC -> Clinical history -> Prior treatments failed -> Requested procedure with CPT/ICD-10 -> Literature support -> Urgency statement -> Physician signature block

example_queries: Write a prior auth letter for cardiac catheterization for a 62-year-old with unstable angina, positive stress test, EF 40%, failed medical therapy
Generate prior authorization for cardiac MRI, patient has new CHF diagnosis, echo inconclusive, need tissue characterization

title: Ejection Fraction & Heart Failure Stage Classification
problem: Heart failure classification involves multiple overlapping systems (NYHA class, ACC/AHA stages, LVEF categories) that were updated in 2022 Universal Definition. Quickly determining HFrEF vs HFmrEF vs HFpEF, appropriate stage, and guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) recommendations during a visit requires mental juggling of multiple parameters.
who: All cardiologists managing heart failure patients, especially early-career

skill_spec.name: Heart Failure Classification & GDMT Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Classifies heart failure by EF category, NYHA class, ACC/AHA stage and recommends guideline-directed medical therapy
skill_spec.data_domain: Heart failure classification and GDMT per 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guidelines

data_hints.source_law: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
data_hints.categories: HFrEF (EF<=40%), HFmrEF (EF 41-49%), HFpEF (EF>=50%), HFimpEF (previously reduced, now >40%)

example_queries: Patient has EF 35%, NYHA class III, what's the ACC/AHA stage and recommended GDMT?
What are the four pillars of heart failure therapy for HFrEF and when do I add each one?

title: Anticoagulation for AFib - CHA2DS2-VASc & HAS-BLED Calculator
problem: Every atrial fibrillation patient requires stroke risk (CHA2DS2-VASc) and bleeding risk (HAS-BLED) assessment to decide on anticoagulation. Cardiologists see dozens of AFib patients weekly and must balance stroke prevention against bleeding risk. Calculation errors or forgetting a risk factor can lead to inappropriate therapy - either a preventable stroke or a major bleed.
who: All cardiologists managing atrial fibrillation patients

skill_spec.name: AFib Anticoagulation Decision Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED scores with anticoagulation recommendation per ACC/AHA guidelines

inputs.name: vascular_disease
inputs.label: Vascular disease (prior MI, PAD, aortic plaque)?

outputs.name: recommendation
outputs.label: Anticoagulation recommendation per 2023 ACC/AHA AFib guidelines

skill_spec.formula_hint: CHA2DS2-VASc: CHF=1, HTN=1, Age>=75=2, DM=1, Stroke=2, Vasc=1, Age65-74=1, Female=1. HAS-BLED: HTN=1, Renal=1, Liver=1, Stroke=1, Bleeding=1, Labile INR=1, Age>65=1, Drugs=1, Alcohol=1. Males: anticoag if >=2. Females: anticoag if >=3.

example_queries: CHA2DS2-VASc for 72-year-old woman with hypertension and diabetes, no prior stroke
Should I anticoagulate a 68-year-old male with lone AFib, no other risk factors? Calculate both stroke and bleeding risk

title: Board Recertification & MOC Tracking Checklist
problem: ABIM Maintenance of Certification (MOC) requires tracking CME credits, self-assessment modules, practice improvement activities, and exam scheduling across multi-year cycles. The new ABCVM pathway adds complexity. Failure to maintain certification risks hospital privileges, insurance panel participation, and career advancement. Many cardiologists scramble at deadline.
who: All board-certified cardiologists, especially mid-career and senior

skill_spec.name: Board MOC Tracker Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step checklist for ABIM cardiovascular disease MOC requirements with timeline and deadlines
steps: Step 1: Verify current ABIM certification status and expiration date at abim.org
Step 2: Confirm CME credit requirements - minimum 100 points per 5-year cycle, including at least 20 self-assessment points
Step 3: Complete required Knowledge Check-In (KCI) or traditional exam by deadline - 5-year rolling cycle
Step 4: Log qualifying CME activities (ACC, AHA, ASE courses count for ABIM credit)
Step 5: Complete at least one Practice Improvement Module or Quality Improvement activity
Step 6: Verify state medical license is current and matches ABIM records
Step 7: Evaluate ABCVM alternative certification pathway if applicable
Step 8: Submit attestation of medical licensure and hospital privileges
Step 9: Pay MOC fees (budget ~$220/year for ABIM)
Step 10: Document completion and save certificates for hospital credentialing
warnings: Warning: ABIM certification lapses if MOC requirements not met by expiration - reinstatement requires full exam
Warning: Many hospitals require active board certification for privileges - lapsed cert = lost privileges
Warning: Some states now require MOC participation for license renewal

example_queries: My ABIM cardiovascular certification expires in 18 months, what do I need to complete?
What's the difference between ABIM MOC and the new ABCVM certification?

title: STEMI & Acute Coronary Syndrome Response Checklist
problem: STEMI and ACS management requires rapid, protocol-driven decisions under extreme time pressure - door-to-balloon time must be <90 minutes. Missing a step in the acute phase (dual antiplatelet loading, anticoagulation, cath lab activation, contraindication screening) can be fatal. Even experienced cardiologists benefit from a systematic checklist during high-stress acute events.
who: All cardiologists on call and managing acute cardiac events

skill_spec.name: ACS/STEMI Response Protocol
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step acute coronary syndrome management protocol from ER presentation through cath lab and post-PCI care
steps: Step 1: Confirm STEMI on 12-lead ECG (ST elevation >=1mm in 2+ contiguous leads, or new LBBB)
Step 2: Activate cath lab - note door time, target D2B <90 min (or <120 min if transfer)
Step 3: Aspirin 325mg chewed (if not already given) + P2Y12 inhibitor loading (ticagrelor 180mg or prasugrel 60mg preferred over clopidogrel 600mg)
Step 4: Anticoagulation - heparin bolus 60 U/kg (max 4000 U) + infusion or bivalirudin per protocol
Step 5: Check contraindications: active bleeding, recent surgery, known allergy, prior ICH, severe thrombocytopenia
Step 6: Beta-blocker if no cardiogenic shock, decompensated HF, or bradycardia (metoprolol 5mg IV x3 prn)
Step 7: Obtain emergency labs: troponin, CBC, BMP, coagulation, type & screen
Step 8: Proceed to cath lab - perform coronary angiography and PCI of culprit lesion
Step 9: Post-PCI: confirm TIMI-3 flow, document stent details, start DAPT plan
Step 10: Admit CCU, serial troponins q6h, echo within 24-48h, initiate GDMT (ACEi/ARB, beta-blocker, high-intensity statin)
warnings: Warning: Do NOT delay cath for additional testing in clear STEMI
Warning: Prasugrel contraindicated if prior stroke/TIA or age >=75 or weight <60kg
Warning: Check for fibrinolytic eligibility if PCI not available within 120 minutes

example_queries: STEMI just came in, 55-year-old male, walk me through the acute protocol step by step
Patient presenting with NSTEMI, troponin 0.8, what's the management checklist? High risk features?

Burnout leads to medical errors, early retirement, and worsens the projected 17% cardiologist shortage by 2035. Many cardiologists don't recognize burnout until it's severe.
who: All cardiologists, especially mid-career with heavy clinical loads

skill_spec.expertise_area: Physician burnout assessment, practice efficiency optimization, delegation strategies, and workload management specific to cardiology
